optionDefaults: Defaults below are schema defaults. defaultFrom records source-level fallback to another option when omitted; sourceDefault/sourceFlags record differing source literals. Schema constraints and enums remain authoritative except documented source discrepancies.

fixabilityMeaning.safe: A structural or whitespace transformation exists; still preserve meaning, protected regions, and configured exceptions.
fixabilityMeaning.conditional: Some violations can be repaired, but ambiguous intent, semantic changes, configuration conflicts, or preservation requirements can require diagnostics instead.
fixabilityMeaning.diagnostic-only: No general safe automatic repair within the agreed scope.

rules.rationale: Changing heading levels guesses document hierarchy.
Convert heading syntax without changing levels; pure setext cannot represent levels 3–6.
Normalize unordered markers while retaining nesting and list boundaries.
Adjust sibling indentation only when item ownership remains unchanged.
Reindent list containers and continuations without changing code or nesting.
Remove incidental spaces; preserve hard breaks, tables, and code semantics even when a lint remains.
Tab substitution can change nesting or code strings; require semantic safety and preserve tables.
Repair confidently recognized reversed syntax; it changes rendering and may be literal prose.
Reduce blank runs outside literal regions without merging distinct blocks or lists.
Reflow prose with indivisible inline links/code; preserve tables and headings; code needs a formatter; unbreakable tokens may remain.
Removing shell prompt markers requires recognizing examples, not literal code content.
Inserting a space can turn literal text into a heading; ambiguous cases remain diagnostic.
Normalize opening heading separator whitespace.
Repair intended closed headings only when literal content is not reinterpreted.
Normalize closed heading separator whitespace.
Adjust surrounding blanks without changing front matter or enclosing block meaning.
Remove heading indentation only when container ownership is preserved.
Renaming or deleting headings invents content and changes anchors.
Selecting the document title requires author intent.

The user authorizes the rule-prescribed punctuation removal when enabled, including by default. Respect configured characters and upstream entity/emoji exceptions; do not block the fix solely because heading text changes.
Normalize quote spacing without reinterpreting nested code or lists.
A blank between quotes may intentionally separate quotations.
Normalize numbering while preserving rendered start values and container structure.
Update marker spacing and continuation indentation together.
Insert surrounding blanks without changing list tightness or literal code.
Add block separators only when they preserve rendered structure.
Removing or escaping HTML can change meaning or presentation.
Wrap an unambiguous URL as an autolink without changing destination or table source.
Normalize a parsed thematic break while preserving block boundaries.
Choosing a heading level or replacing intentional emphasis guesses intent.
Repair intended emphasis only when delimiters are not literal prose.
Strip only syntax padding; code-span whitespace may be meaningful.
Label trimming must not alter meaningful text; tables stay unchanged.
Do not guess a missing language or discard potentially meaningful info-string attributes.
A missing title cannot be invented or existing prose reclassified safely.
A destination must be supplied by the author.
Required structure does not authorize inserting or rearranging content.
Configured capitalization may be unambiguous in prose, but code identifiers and URLs must not be rewritten blindly.
Meaningful image descriptions require author input.
Convert code containers only when content, info strings, and nested block boundaries survive.
Normalize EOF outside unterminated literal regions where adding a newline can change content.
Choose fence characters and lengths that cannot close inside content or invalidate the info string.
Delimiter changes must preserve parsed emphasis, including intraword restrictions; tables remain untouched.
Delimiter changes must preserve parsed strong emphasis and leave table source intact.
Only uniquely determined fragment corrections are safe; do not guess targets or edit tables.
An undefined reference requires a destination, not a fabricated definition.
Removing unused definitions discards source content; only demonstrably redundant duplicate definitions qualify for safe removal.
Only meaning-preserving conversions consistent with inline-link preservation are allowed; never convert existing inline links to references.
Preserve table source even when its pipe style violates configuration.
Preserve tables; adding or deleting cells also requires author intent.
Surrounding blank lines may change without editing table rows if block structure remains unchanged.
A useful replacement label requires author input.
Preserve table source, including column spacing and delimiters.
